{"id":"guide:kmp-agent:advanced:repository","kind":"instruction","text":"## Memory can live in the repository

Project-scoped embedded writes maintain `.kmp/memory.jsonl` automatically and
atomically before returning success. The store itself (`.kernel/`) is machine
state and stays gitignored — the bundle is a different thing, and committing
it is what makes a fresh clone arrive with the project's decisions instead of
an empty memory. `kmp-mcp export` is the explicit repair/checkpoint command;
`kmp-mcp import` reads the bundle into an empty store.

If `doctor` reports a pending export, stop other KMP sessions, run the normal
export and inspect its diff, then use `kmp-mcp export --repair-pending` to
acknowledge recovery. The normal export intentionally does not clear an
in-flight marker that could belong to another SQLite writer.

It is one JSON object per line in sequence order, so an append-only log
appears in `git diff` as appended lines. A session that recorded three
decisions is three new lines plus the header update, and each line carries who
wrote it and the rationale of every relation, verbatim. The format-2 header
names the snapshot, creation time, event range, about coverage and SHA-256, so
a saved copy can be verified before restore.

Use named snapshots when a release or risky change needs a recovery point:

```bash
kmp-mcp snapshot create pre-release
kmp-mcp snapshot verify pre-release
kmp-mcp snapshot read pre-release kmp_goto \
  '{"about":"project:kmp","at":{"sequence":12}}'
```

The read happens in an isolated temporary store and cannot call either writer.
For two branches, `kmp-mcp snapshot merge <left> <right> <new-name>` only
fast-forwards an exact prefix. A divergence is a semantic conflict: never
hand-interleave the JSONL lines.

Two limits to state rather than discover. **Import requires an empty store**:
it is restore, not merge, because replaying a bundle over existing memory
could duplicate history or interleave two timelines and neither has an answer
the kernel could pick. And **a bundle carries the payloads as written** — a
secret in memory is a secret in the committed file, so the hygiene of the

{"id":"guide:kmp-agent:advanced:errors","kind":"instruction","text":"## When the tools are not there

If the kmp tools are missing from your inventory, do not silently
fall back to re-deriving everything — say so. The usual causes are specific
and fixable, and `/kmp:doctor` distinguishes them:

- the `kmp-mcp` binary is not installed or not on `PATH`;
- the session started before the binary, plugin, or MCP registration changed,
  so it is still carrying the old tool inventory — restart the session;
- the configured binary or data directory no longer exists — run
  `/kmp:doctor` to identify the stale path.

## Errors

Tool failures set `isError=true` and carry
`structuredContent.error.{code,message}`. Read the code; it is produced where
the failure happened, never inferred from the words, and `tools/list` carries
the closed set under `_meta."kmp/errorCodes"` with what each one means.

| code | what to do |
| --- | --- |
| `invalid_argument` | fix the arguments — retrying unchanged cannot work |
| `not_found` | the requested about or ref was not found; check the exact address and selected store before inferring absence |
| `conflict` | inspect the message: retryable concurrency conflicts are safe to replay with the same key; a key accepted with different content must not be reused |
| `unavailable` | the kernel was unreachable; the same call may work later |
| `unknown_tool` | no such tool here |
| `backend_error` | the kernel failed for a reason no argument can fix |

An unknown argument is refused rather than dropped: every tool declares
`additionalProperties: false` and the boundary enforces it, so a misspelling
comes back naming the key instead of being answered from defaults.

complete `{tool, arguments}` calls to the relevant verb and worked lessons.
Read the field and code in every feedback item first; reuse lessons already in
context and consult only the missing explanation. The help is also available in
the text fallback. It does not replace `feedback[].action`, which can inspect
a missing prerequisite or restart a stale selection. Neither help nor a lesson
authorizes writing invented evidence or widening the task's scope.

source to correct the observation time; do not substitute today's time merely

history, where the relation has its own why and evidence. If the source does not
justify that relation, the lesson cannot supply its proof.

failed reads of the agent guide do not suggest reading the guide again. An Ask

{"id":"guide:kmp-agent:example:four-clocks","kind":"instruction","text":"# Worked example: four clocks and zoom to the proof

Use this fictional Atlas permit to separate when a decision was signed, when
the reviewer received it, when KMP recorded it and when it applied. The LLM
interprets the sources; KMP preserves the chosen coordinates. A fact that
applied before it was reported is not evidence that the reviewer knew it then.
If a source says only “this state was observed today; its onset is unknown”,
record its observation and omit `valid_from`. Do not turn today's observation
into an invented start, or copy a later report's boundary into earlier knowledge.

Read the installed guide/AGENT.md and its exact reference to this lesson in
guide:kmp-agent. Consult time, writer, lifecycle and audit guidance when used.
Run only in the isolated about `example:guide:four-clocks`. This authored replay
checks the protocol; it does not measure an LLM's judgment on unseen sources.

## Resolve a real calendar before writing

Read the real UTC clock once. D4 is that UTC calendar day; D1, D2 and D3 are
three, two and one days earlier. D5 is the following midnight. In this synthetic
case, the archived reports become available together on D4. Preserve the source
reviewer's historical observation times. Ingestion is the real kernel commit
on D4, not an input the LLM fills in. If the run crosses UTC midnight, record
that fact and start a new isolated run with a new calendar.

For example, a run on September 8 uses September 5 as D1, September 6 as D2,
September 7 as D3 and September 9 as D5. Never send those sample dates blindly.
The replay reads the real clock and records the following `clock` bindings:

| Binding | Resolved UTC time |
| --- | --- |
| day1 | D1 00:00 |
| occurred | D1 09:00 |
| checked | D1 09:15 |
| day2 | D2 00:00, also the interval's exclusive end |
| day3 | D3 00:00 |
| observed | D3 14:00 |
| check_observed | D3 14:15 |
| receipt_observed | D3 14:30 |
| day4 | D4 00:00 |
| day5 | D5 00:00, exclusive validity end |

`${clock.occurred}` is a local calendar binding, not a tool result. Other
`${name...}` values copy returned results. Envelopes name `tool`, `arguments`
and `save_as`; send only arguments. The sources below use the same resolved
calendar. `expect_error` identifies an intentional refusal. Complete every
returned continuation before claiming a complete selection; this tiny story
fits its explicit limits and the replay stops if a page is incomplete.

## Sources available to the writer

All source text is fictional and literal within this scenario. The writer
gets these documents and the calendar, not the later reader's questions.

| Source | Occurred | First observed by reviewer | Literal source |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| S1, signed permit | D1 09:00 | D3 14:00 | Permit TEMP-4 allows Atlas to retry failed uploads from D2 00:00 UTC until D5 00:00 UTC, exclusive. |
| S2, signature check | D1 09:15 | D3 14:15 | CHECK-4 verifies the signature of permit TEMP-4 and the validity dates printed on it. |
| S3, delivery receipt | D2 00:00 | D3 14:30 | RECEIPT-4 confirms delivery of permit TEMP-4 to the Atlas operations mailbox. |

S1 is a decision with a stated validity interval. S2 is an observation about
signature verification, not an extension of that validity. S3 is feedback
confirming delivery, not approval of the permission or proof that the reviewer
read it at delivery time. Only S1 gets `valid_from` and `valid_until`.

## Coordinate ownership

The entry's `coordinates` already create its `contains_entry` memberships.
Do not add another structural link just to put it on a label. If a canonical
packet repeats `contains_entry` without a coordinate, KMP reuses the matching
coordinate of the entry in that same packet, including its assigned sequence
and ingestion clock. Without a matching membership it refuses the write
before commit. For an existing memory, use `kmp_relabel` to change labels;
an explicit membership link must carry its coordinate. A missing coordinate
must never erase a memory's existing clocks.

## Guidance during work

Pass `context_id` with memory and viewer calls. It is interaction metadata,
removed before the memory operation, its hash or pagination contract. It does
not grant access. Writer and Relabel may omit actor when this context supplies
the persistent name; an explicit actor takes precedence.

Before an unfamiliar operation, request its topic card and consult the linked
verb/examples you need. A valid first operation is never blocked merely because
a delivery mark is absent. Help returned after an operation cannot prevent a
mistake already made. If uncertain, ask `kmp_guide` explicitly even if a topic
was served before.

A work result adds one JSON text block containing `kmp_guidance`. The original
structuredContent, proof, receipt and their byte budget stay unchanged. The
extra block has its own context cost; consumers must pass it through to the
agent. It is not duplicated in _meta. No context means no automatic usage block.

`usage` counts observed calls, refusals and protocol UNKNOWNs; it is not a
learning score or a count of committed writes. A retry may count as another call
while idempotency still keeps one memory. `usage.recorded=false` means metadata
failed: keep the original operation result and never repeat a write just to fix
usage accounting. `served` records requested cards and exact guide/example refs
whose bodies were actually returned with context. A suggested link or reused
object without text does not count. An observed asset revision change starts a
new delivery view; ordinary work reports the last seen revision and does not
pretend to know an unread guide has changed.

Set optional `purpose` to `continue` (default), `audit`, `history` or `answer`.
The recommendation uses typed result fields in this order:

| Situation | Suggested move |
| --- | --- |
| Refusal with executable feedback | Review the producer's repair or restart |
| Partial packet | Execute the native continuation, preserving selection |
| Semantic UNKNOWN after completing the packet | Stop within that selection |
| History with native next action | Use its clock and dimensions for a new selection |
| History from current Inspect | Consult time guidance and choose a clock |
| Audit of declared links in Inspect | Trace one stored relation and assess why/evidence |
| Audit/answer from single-about recall | Inspect a canonical claim ref as a fresh current read |

The link choice has stable lexical order, not an importance score. Alternatives
remain in the original response. `basis` points to the fields used;
`changes_selection` identifies a fresh read. An inspection suggested after

{"id":"guide:kmp:advanced:clocks","kind":"concept","text":"The difference between occurred and observed time is the event boundary versus the knowledge boundary. {"id":"guide:kmp:advanced:budgets","kind":"concept","text":"budget.max_bytes limits how much structured response a host receives. If a valid ceiling is smaller than KMP's minimal honest response, KMP returns that stable floor with a warning naming both sizes instead of failing or hiding the canonical object. Values below 512 bytes are invalid; raise the ceiling only when you need richer detail. A cited memory stays identifiable when its preview is shortened. Ask and Wake now return the complete call for continuing or restoring a shortened preview. A restoration starts a new read with enough bytes; its agent discards the partial reconstruction. It can also inspect the cited memory for its full text. Finishing expansion alone does not prove the preview is complete. An optional local semantic encoder can help the embedded engine find differently worded sources. Similarity is shown as retrieval evidence and never establishes an answer on its own; an unavailable encoder leaves ordinary retrieval available with a warning. Ask keeps cited memories first and returns additional evidence in retrieval order, including when it spans several pages. If a page cannot fit the next item, KMP says that it cannot advance: allow a larger response or keep the result explicitly partial. An agent that retained the first inspected object can request later pages with page.repeat_object=false. KMP sends its ref and the remaining proof, marks object_reused, and rejects the continuation if the object or selected evidence changed. Registered agents can receive a short continuation identifier instead of copying a long call. It retains one exact read, including the next-page budget. Replay repeats that page; its next action advances. These bounded metadata records survive reconnect but are not durable memory or access permissions. Missing or expired identifiers require a fresh read; the complete action remains available when a short identifier cannot be retained. A host can opt into sharing repeated passages. The response then prints an identical passage once and refers to it from each original record. Source identity, authorship, times and support remain distinct even when wording is equal. The agent resolves short passage names and citation names using separate tables in that response, then cites the original memory or evidence ref. The original record definitions stay explicit; a short citation never combines source identities. This only changes presentation: it does not merge facts, certify a complete proof or silently discard qualifiers. Partly overlapping quotations remain separate when source boundaries are not known. A host can also compose captured read groups using kmp-mcp context project, and restore admitted groups with context expand. Neither command opens memory. If the host knows a quote’s exact source and boundaries, overlapping quotes may share ordered fragments. The reader joins those fragments without adding words or separators; source identities remain separate. An omitted source stays omitted, and its read remains listed. This saves representation space only when the complete encoding is smaller; it does not establish a complete proof.","coordinates":[{"dimension":"timeline","scope_id":"label:v1:guide%3Akmp:timeline:timeline","occurred_at":"unix:101787875620:000000000","observed_at":"unix:101787875620:000000000","ingested_at":"unix:101789092841:737561506","sequence":8},{"dimension":"audience","scope_id":"label:v1:guide%3Akmp:audience:audience-person","ingested_at":"unix:101789092841:737561506","sequence":8},{"dimension":"depth","scope_id":"label:v1:guide%3Akmp:depth:depth-advanced","ingested_at":"unix:101789092841:737561506","sequence":8}],"metadata":{"audience":"person","depth":"advanced","guide_revision":"097a59f7d40640a8c33b9191cdf2d244ce51298a5f03007f2bd1fb0df358dce3","guide_version":"1","source":"editorial"}}

{"id":"guide:kmp:advanced:decision-history","kind":"instruction","text":"A decision can change without losing its history. In the worked Atlas example, offline work is required on September 1; SQLite is chosen for that reason on September 2. A central shared journal is required on September 5, and a later explicit decision replaces SQLite with PostgreSQL. The agent guide entry guide:kmp-agent:example:decision-history contains the sources and complete calls. Ask your agent to run this fictional example in an isolated store and open its about example:guide:decision-history in ChronoLoom. Select the new decision at Memories detail: one evidential link explains what it replaces, and one motivational link explains why it was chosen. Follow each to its original evidence. Compare September 3 with September 6 using an explicit clock; the new choice must not be projected into the past. Two memory kinds and two relation classes are justified by these sources. This lesson does not cover every kind or relationship, nor establish that a new writer LLM has learned to use KMP.","coordinates":[{"dimension":"timeline","scope_id":"label:v1:guide%3Akmp:timeline:timeline","occurred_at":"unix:101787876040:000000000","observed_at":"unix:101787876040:000000000","ingested_at":"unix:101789092841:737561506","sequence":15},{"dimension":"audience","scope_id":"label:v1:guide%3Akmp:audience:audience-person","ingested_at":"unix:101789092841:737561506","sequence":15},{"dimension":"depth","scope_id":"label:v1:guide%3Akmp:depth:depth-advanced","ingested_at":"unix:101789092841:737561506","sequence":15}],"metadata":{"audience":"person","depth":"advanced","guide_revision":"097a59f7d40640a8c33b9191cdf2d244ce51298a5f03007f2bd1fb0df358dce3","guide_version":"1","source":"editorial"}}

{"id":"guide:kmp:advanced:alias-ownership","kind":"instruction","text":"An alias is not an account owner. In the second worked example, a signed source identifies Elena Vega as Nora, while an unqualified visitor-log mention of Nora remains unresolved. Separately, the account @oak is assigned to Jon and later to Rui. The assignment is replaced; Jon and Rui remain distinct people. Ask your agent to open the isolated example:guide:alias-ownership story in ChronoLoom after reading guide:kmp-agent:example:alias-ownership. Follow the same_entity_as link for the proven alias and the supersedes link for the account change; inspect their sources. Filtering the label Nora also includes the unidentified visitor, so a label is not identity proof. The example uses three observations and two assignment decisions because the sources justify them. {"id":"guide:kmp:advanced:distributed-incident","kind":"instruction","text":"INC-17 contains an outage EVT-17-F and its later recovery EVT-17-R. Support reports the outage first; project later audits that same outage. Ask the agent to read guide:kmp-agent:example:distributed-incident and run it in an isolated store. Open example:guide:incident-support in ChronoLoom and add example:guide:incident-project to the projection. Compare the initial observed view on September 1 with the late audit and reconciliation on September 2. Two observations, an error path and a success path have distinct roles. Shared labels find candidate pairs; the source-backed same_event_as link identifies only the two outage reports. Select its new support declaration, follow the edge and inspect its literal evidence. The recovery remains a separate event. Switch from observed to occurred to see why evidence learned on September 2 can describe an event on September 1; do not infer earlier knowledge from the event clock. The two abouts keep their original texts and ownership. This authored native example does not measure a new LLM writer.","coordinates":[{"dimension":"timeline","scope_id":"label:v1:guide%3Akmp:timeline:timeline","occurred_at":"unix:101787876160:000000000","observed_at":"unix:101787876160:000000000","ingested_at":"unix:101789092841:737561506","sequence":17},{"dimension":"audience","scope_id":"label:v1:guide%3Akmp:audience:audience-person","ingested_at":"unix:101789092841:737561506","sequence":17},{"dimension":"depth","scope_id":"label:v1:guide%3Akmp:depth:depth-advanced","ingested_at":"unix:101789092841:737561506","sequence":17}],"metadata":{"audience":"person","depth":"advanced","guide_revision":"097a59f7d40640a8c33b9191cdf2d244ce51298a5f03007f2bd1fb0df358dce3","guide_version":"1","source":"editorial"}}

{"id":"guide:kmp:advanced:four-clocks","kind":"instruction","text":"The TEMP-4 permit is signed on day one, first observed by a reviewer on day three and recorded by KMP on the real execution day four. It applies from day two until day five, exclusive. Ask the agent to read guide:kmp-agent:example:four-clocks and resolve its calendar before running the isolated example:guide:four-clocks. Start in ChronoLoom at Atlas, narrow the occurred window, then choose Moment to inspect the permit and the signature check that supports it.
